failure_reason: The missing_index injection did not remove a truly critical index used by the active TPC-C query mix, so rows examined did not increase (>2x) and the optimizer did not switch to a full table scan (EXPLAIN access_type=ALL). As a result, p95 latency did not rise enough and QPS did not drop. Likely causes: (1) the dropped index was redundant or not on a hot predicate; (2) statistics were not refreshed after DDL so the optimizer still chose a range/ref plan; and/or (3) the workload did not sufficiently exercise the affected queries (ORDER-STATUS and PAYMENT by last name) to push p95 and QPS thresholds. If your workload node is not injected/configurable, you will need to add or adjust it to bias toward affected queries; otherwise downstream nodes will remain weak even with the correct index dropped.
suggested_changes: Retarget the missing_index action to the ORDERS secondary index used by ORDER-STATUS: drop the composite index on (o_w_id, o_d_id, o_c_id, o_id). Example SQL: ALTER TABLE orders DROP INDEX idx_orders_wdc_cid_oid; then ANALYZE TABLE orders; (Replace idx_orders_wdc_cid_oid with the actual index name from SHOW INDEX FROM orders.)
Immediately refresh optimizer statistics after the DDL so plans reflect the missing index: ANALYZE TABLE orders; (and ANALYZE TABLE customer; if you also change customer indexes).

Increase workload pressure on the affected code paths to raise p95 and cause a visible QPS drop: raise terminals/concurrency and skew the transaction mix toward ORDER-STATUS and PAYMENT-by-last-name. For example: terminals=128, duration_sec=300, transaction_mix: order_status=0.35, payment_by_last_name=0.45, new_order=0.15, others=0.05. If the workload generator is not an injected node in this experiment, you will need to add one to apply these changes.
Ensure a stable baseline and sufficient injection window for ratio-based detectors: baseline >= 60s, injection >= 240–300s, keep overall request rate stable across baseline and injection.

If EXPLAIN access_type still does not show ALL after dropping the ORDERS customer index, verify you targeted the correct index (via SHOW INDEX FROM orders) and that the ORDER-STATUS query text matches the index columns. If necessary, also drop the CUSTOMER last-name index on (c_w_id, c_d_id, c_last, c_first, c_id) to amplify rows examined in PAYMENT-by-last-name. Note: this may still yield a range scan via PK on (c_w_id, c_d_id, c_id); therefore biasing ORDER-STATUS is more reliable for triggering ALL.
Warm up caches before baseline (e.g., 30–60s) so that changes in rows examined and latency reflect plan differences rather than cold caches.

If your harness supports session-level SQL in the workload script, run ANALYZE TABLE orders immediately after the DROP INDEX within the same phase/session to avoid stale stats. Avoid global optimizer tweaks; rely on stats and index removal to induce poor plans.
Verify that the dropped index remains absent for the entire injection duration (no automatic rebuild/revert) and that the DDL completed before measurement begins.

missing_index.drop_index_sql: ALTER TABLE orders DROP INDEX idx_orders_wdc_cid_oid; ANALYZE TABLE orders;

risk_warning: On a tpcc_10W dataset, dropping critical secondary indexes on ORDERS (and especially on CUSTOMER) can cause very long scans, spikes in transaction latency, lock contention, and potential replication lag. ANALYZE TABLE is online but may cause transient overhead. Only run in non-production, verify adequate disk/redo capacity, and have a rollback plan (CREATE INDEX on the exact dropped index) ready before injection.
